sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A medium-sized to rather large species, closely related to M. kalgoorliensis, from which it differs as follows: it is smaller and slightly more hairy; the ocelli are smaller and farther from the compound eyes; the fontanelle consists of a small oval anterior pore and a small, separate, spherical, nearly black posterior part (not a long slender slit as in the Western Australian species); antennal segment 3 is the smallest; the pronotum (Fig. 298) is narrower and longer, and the posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum are narrower and distinctly more deeply notched. Measurements (mm): length with wings 11.00—11.50; length without wings 6.00—6.50; head length (to apex of labrum) defective in the original OCR and not transcribed; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.57—0.66; head width 1.13—1.24; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.29—0.32; ocellus length 0.12—0.13; pronotum length 0.75—0.84; pronotum width 1.13—1.28; fore wing length 9.00—9.50; fore wing width 2.70.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original combination is Mirotermes insitivus Hill, 1929, now placed in Invasitermes. Measurements in mm. Distribution: Townsville, northern Queensland. The original records the species only from alates, taken at Townsville Town Common in two successive seasons; soldier and worker are still unknown. In 1919—1920 and 1920—1921, from September to February of the following year (months 9 and 2), many nests still occupied by Eutermes magnus contained large numbers of first-form nymphs and alates of this species, the inquiline and its host sharing the same galleries, and the species has no soldiers or workers of its own. The type specimen is in the National Museum of Victoria. OCR problems: the line for head length (to apex of labrum) is severely defective, reading "lm rr ~ I'2 1 ' 21" in the original, and cannot be reliably restored, so this measurement is left blank; "(Pig/ 298)" is a misreading of Fig.; "Luring" is a misreading of During; "Mirotermee" is a misreading of Mirotermes.
